text.headline: Gold slides as inflation data weighs
text.tone: Precious metals and equities retreated as confirmed inflation data and hawkish policy signals influenced market sentiment during Thursday's session.
lead: Gold fell 2.7% on Thursday, marking a notable decline alongside other precious metals. Silver dropped 4.4% and platinum lost 3.2% on the [[metals|Hard Assets Terminal]]. These moves coincided with a retreat in US large caps, while the EB Shariah US 100 fell 2.3% in the latest [[Islamic|Islamic Investment]] data.

The downward pressure is consistent with confirmed reports of hotter inflation, which appears to be driving expectations for a more hawkish Federal Reserve. Markets are pricing in the possibility of further rate hikes, a scenario that typically weighs on non-yielding assets. Bitcoin also fell, behaving like a risk asset rather than a safe haven in this environment.

Industrial demand concerns may also be playing a role. Silver and platinum fell in tandem with copper, a pattern often linked to softer expectations for manufacturing. However, the [[outlook|Market Outlook]] notes that while commodities are under pressure, oil and gas themes have remained resilient this quarter.

The next sessions will clarify if this sell-off reflects a lasting shift in inflation expectations. Continued weakness in metals alongside rising yields would strengthen the hawkish policy interpretation. Conversely, a stabilization in equities might suggest the move was a short-term reaction to specific data points.

briefs.markets: US large caps fell 2.2% on Thursday, while the 30-year Treasury yield dropped 5 bp to 5.41% in latest data on the [[markets|Financial Markets]] page.
briefs.energy: Energy prices were mixed in latest data, with US natural gas falling 3.1% to $3.10 while Brent crude remained flat at $92.94 on the [[energy|Energy Terminal]].
briefs.crypto: Bitcoin fell 1.9% to $61,813 as the total crypto market cap declined 4.4%, with digital assets tracking equity weakness on the [[crypto|Crypto & Currencies]] terminal.
briefs.metals: Silver led the retreat in hard assets with a 4.4% drop to $42.41, while copper fell 1.4% to $12,570/t on the [[metals|Hard Assets Terminal]].
briefs.estate: The [[estate|Estate Index]] shows global divergence, with Moldova rising 33.7% while China fell 6.3%, reflecting varied national housing market conditions.
briefs.corporate: The [[corporate|Corporate Monitor]] identifies APA Corporation as a top-scoring firm with a score of 89, amid a broader risk-on regime for credit spreads.
briefs.outlook: The [[outlook|Market Outlook]] highlights significant quarterly weakness in semiconductors and AI themes, even as oil and gas assets gained 2.2% over the same period.
briefs.islamic: The EB Shariah US 100 fell 2.3% to 110.47, though it maintains a year-to-date lead over conventional benchmarks on the [[islamic|Islamic Investment]] page.

watch: Crypto regulation and flows as news volume is 3.63x normal, though Bitcoin has yet to show a distinct reaction to recent custodian changes.
US budget and debt developments following reports of war funding disputes, which could impact the term premium on long-dated Treasury yields.
The gold-silver ratio, currently at 84.6, to see if industrial demand concerns continue to push silver lower relative to other precious metals.
